findings.description: async retry_any.__ror__ checks `isinstance(other, retry_all)` when it should check `retry_any`. This is the wrong class, so it flattens the wrong thing.
findings.rationale: Trigger: `retry_all(a, b) | async_retry_any(c, d)`. The check matches and `retry_any(a, b, c, d)` is built, which turns an AND into an OR and silently changes retry semantics. Conversely, `retry_any(a, b) | async_retry_any(c, d)` is not flattened.
